tasks.enabler_now: Native equipment fields can reduce repeated entry and routing lookup.
tasks.still_hard: Actual symptoms and immediate machine condition need observation.
tasks.human_edge: The operator distinguishes an observed malfunction from an unverified diagnosis.
tasks.altitude: Less notice administration; fault observation stays human.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native machine/contact fields can support malfunction notices; they do not observe or diagnose the malfunction.

assumptions: Operator produces actual symptoms/status in retained s1; actual equipment owner supplies identifiers and service contacts. S3 reduces repeated stable fields only and retains new symptom capture and complete final checking.

Scenario is actual written notification, not a mandatory ticket for every oral call. Oral-only notification retains actual talk and readiness judgement, removes unused written-entry branch and reweights. No maintenance outcome is inferred from notice delivery; repair staff labour excluded.

Shares are provisional, not measured. Native functions first; existing prefill earns zero saving. Actual notification retains one percent using existing final checking; no saving assigned to send or added self-approval work.
unknowns: Is a written malfunction notice actually required?
research_questions: Can native fields reduce repeated identifiers after complete symptom checking?
